Victoria axes Commonwealth Games plans due to financial constraints, Daniel Andrews confirms — as it happened

Victoria axes Commonwealth Games plans due to financial constraints, Daniel Andrews confirms — as it happened

  • T

    By Tim Callanan

  • By Georgie Hewson

  • By Judd Boaz

  • By Ashleigh Barraclough

  • Topic:Sport

Posted Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 9:13amTue 18 Jul 2023 at 9:13amTue 18 Jul 2023 at 9:13am, updated Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:55pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:55pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:55pm

Victorian Premier Daniel Andrews has confirmed the state will no longer host the Commonwealth Games in 2026.

Look back on our coverage as it happened.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:36pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:36pm

We're leaving the live blog here

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

We'll leave our live coverage here, thanks for following along.

The key takeaways are:

  • Victoria will no longer host the 2026 Commonwealth Games
  • The government said the estimated cost blew out from $2.6 billion to at least $6 billion
  • Regional communities will still get promised sporting facilities and infrastructure
  • Some of the saved money will go to a $1 billion social and affordable housing fund for regional communities

 You can read a wrap of today's events by my colleague Judd Boaz here:

Australian sport left in limbo as Victoria pulls the pin on billions-over-budget Commonwealth Games

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:34pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:34pm

Athletes likely 'going to look at alternative competitions', Leisel Jones says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Former swimming champion Leisel Jones said she was in shock when she heard today's news.

"It was really tricky to get my mind around the concept of actually having a Commonwealth Games cancelled," she said.

"It looks like this is the first time we're going to have it cancelled."

Jones said the Commonwealth Games was often a good opportunity for emerging athletes to make their first team.

"It's going to be a really disappointing decision for a lot of up-and-coming athletes," she said.

"I'm sure there's a lot of organisations around Australia and a lot of sporting committees that are going to look at alternative competitions, because that is a big gap in someone's program."

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:00pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 6:00pm

'We are committed to finding a resolution', Petria Thomas says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Petria Thomas, chef de mission for the Australian Commonwealth Games team, said while the news was "extremely disappointing", she looked forward to a new host being found.

As chef de mission, Thomas is in charge of the Australian contingent to the Games.

"This is a significant blow to the hundreds of athletes and their support teams working toward qualification for a Games here at home – I am thinking of them today", the Olympic gold medalist said.

"We understand the disappointment and the impact this decision will have on their ability to plan and prepare for the Games in 2026, and we are committed to finding a resolution alongside the [Commonwealth Games Federation].

"I remain wholeheartedly committed to providing athletes with every opportunity to represent their country again at a Commonwealth Games."

The Olympic gold medalist swimmer said the Commonwealth Games was the only multi-sport event bringing together able-bodied and para-athletes.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:41pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:41pm

Do the Commonwealth Games still mean something to Australians?

J

By Judd Boaz

As much as I love any sporting spectacle. I think we have to admit that the Commonwealth Games has been in decline for a while. Given no one put their hand up for the 2026 games and Victoria offering to host was a no-contest win at the time, the economic situation around the world has changed dramatically in the last 12 months. Supply issues, Resource issues - no surprise the cost blew out more than anticipated. I think it's the right call to pull out but overall. I do think the time has come to re-evaluate the CG concept and what form it should take, if it is to exist going forward..

The Commonwealth Games is an anachronism that no other country wants. Congratulations to the Premier for deciding that it should not go ahead.

The real issue is that the Commonwealth Games and especially the Olympics are way past their use by dates. So John Coates if you want to host them, you pay for them out of the Commonwealth/ IOC kitty!!!

Our commenters had their own say about what they think the Commonwealth Games mean … or rather don't mean these days.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:39pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:39pm

Victoria will still get housing benefits Games would've provided, Allan says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

The Victorian government has promised $1 billion will be spent on social and affordable housing, using money saved by not hosting the Commonwealth Games.

Jacinta Allan told ABC Radio Melbourne the housing fund was a "massive investment".

"The housing challenges around affordability and availability are as significant in regional Victoria as they are here in Melbourne," she said.

"Why did we want to deliver the Games originally? Because we saw there was an opportunity to make that lasting investment in housing and infrastructure for regional communities — we are still going to do that but without those additional costs that were far greater than any benefits of running a 12-day sporting event."

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:36pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:36pm

Does Victoria's cancellation sound a death knell for the Commonwealth Games?

J

By Judd Boaz

Mary Gearin weighs in on the cancellation of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in regional Victoria, and whether this might be the beginning of the end for the 'Friendly Games'.

Does Victoria's cancellation sound a death knell for the Commonwealth Games?

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:28pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:28pm

Regional sporting facilities will hopefully be delivered by 2026, Allan says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Jacinta Allan said she still wanted the sporting facilities promised to regional areas to be delivered by 2026.

"We have tender processes underway for the deliver of the major competition venues, that we've had to put on pause as a consequence of this decision, and we will need to readjust those settings to go straight to the legacy mode of the infrastructure," she said.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:23pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:23pm

Commonwealth Games budget of $2.6b figured out by consultants, Jacinta Allan says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Jacinta Allan said the higher than expected costs became apparent to the government in recent weeks.

"We've been going through a tender process, we've been going through market soundings, where you're presented with the actuals — not the estimates," she said.

The deputy premier said the original $2.6 billion budget estimate was figured out by consulting firms engaged by the government, including EY.

She said she was not going to blame consultants for the budget blowout.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:13pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 5:13pm

Deputy premier speaking on ABC Radio Melbourne

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Jacinta Allan, Victoria's deputy premier and minister for Commonwealth Games Delivery, is talking to Raf Epstein on ABC Radio Melbourne.

"The budget was set early last year after an assessment of what it would cost to run the Games in 2026, which was $2.6 billion," she said.

"The assessment also factored in that there would be a $3 billion economic benefit to the state as a whole from hosting the Games.

"It became clear that the costs were exceeding $6 billion."

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 4:49pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 4:49pm

Victoria may not 'be trusted' to host future major events, Sam Groth says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Liberal MP and former tennis player Sam Groth said the cancellation of the Games had damaged Victoria's reputation.

Groth, Victoria's shadow minister for Tourism, Sport and Major Events, said the rest of the world would now view Victoria as an unreliable partner to deliver big events.

"This mess raises serious questions about what other major events in Victoria are now under threat," he said.

"For example, is the Boxing Day Test, which Minister Dimopoulos has refused to guarantee, also going to leave Victoria?

"And what about the future of our key events such as the Formula 1 Grand Prix, Australian Open and the 2028 President's Cup? Can Victoria be trusted to continue to deliver these events?

"With this one decision, the Andrews government has sent a signal to the world that Victoria's flagship events are up for grabs and anyone who has a contract to deliver a major event in Melbourne is at risk of having it pulled from under them."

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 4:30pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 4:30pm

Northern Territory not keen to host the Games

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

The Northern Territory will not put its hand up to host the 2026 Commonwealth Games, an NT government spokesperson confirmed.

"The Northern Territory government would welcome any opportunity in supporting the 2026 Commonwealth Games but is not contemplating hosting them," the spokesperson said.

The NT's distinct lack of interest comes after Western Australia, Queensland, Tasmania, New South Wales, the Australian Capital Territory and South Australia also said they were not contemplating making a bid for the Games.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 4:05pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 4:05pm

'Difficult' day for sporting community, Kieren Perkins says

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

Kieren Perkins, former Australian swimmer and CEO of the Australian Sports Commission, is addressing the media about today's events.

The Olympic gold medalist said if a new host was not found for the Games, it would be particularly challenging for less established athletes who use the Games as a springboard for their careers.

"The immediate priority of the Australian Sports Commission is to ensure that our athletes, coaches, high performance and support staff are supported," he said.

He said finding an alternative host would be a challenge.

"To be able to put it together is going to be quite a significant task, and I think this is going to be a very big test for the Commonwealth Games Federation," he said.

Responding to a question about whether the public sees hosting major sporting events as value for money in terms of positive impacts, Perkins said it needed to be an ongoing conversation.

"There is definitely a conversation to be had with the community at large to explain what those impacts are, how they're actually deployed and ... whether it does have a broader community benefit," he said.

"Where large portions of the population don't see that benefit, it probably does ask questions of us of how exactly are we actually deploying the resources that we receive?"

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 3:41pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 3:41pm

What sort of investment will regional Victoria receive in lieu of cancelled 2026 Games?

J

By Judd Boaz

Details were scant in today's press conference about what the $2 billion promised by the government would go towards.

About 1,300 homes costing $1 billion have been promised as part of a Regional Housing Fund.

The government originally earmarked $2.6 billion in the 2022-23 state budget for the Commonwealth Games.

When pressed on this figure by Member for Western Victoria Bev McArthur in June during an Inquiry of the 2023-24 Budget Estimates, Minister for Commonwealth Games Legacy Harriet Shing provided the following indicative split:

The Commonwealth Games is catalysing significant infrastructure investment that will have lasting benefit. For example, the Victorian Government has already announced investment for the development of facilities at Armstrong Creek and Waurn Ponds in Geelong that will see up to $292 million invested into new sporting facilities to host Aquatics, Gymnastics, Weightlifting and Para Powerlifting. Eureka Stadium in Ballarat will receive a $150 million upgrade to ensure it is a worldclass venue for the Commonwealth Games Athletics and Para Athletics, a new athletics track will be built, and the stadium will be expanded to hold an additional 5,000 permanent seats.

It's unknown which of these indicative commitments will be met now that the Games have been scrapped.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 3:32pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 3:32pm

Social sector peak body welcomes funding for housing

A

By Ashleigh Barraclough

The Victorian Council of Social Service (VCOSS) has praised the state government's decision to divert funds from the Games to social housing.

CEO Emma King said the Games were going to deliver thousands of social and affordable housing properties and upgrades to regional sporting facilities and transport infrastructure.

"Securing the housing and social benefits of the Games despite their cancellation is a big win for Victoria," she said.

"Today, Victorian Premier Daniel Andrews has rightly identified housing as our state's 'biggest challenge' and has pledged $1 billion for at least 1,300 additional new housing units.

"More social and affordable housing for Victoria is unequivocally good news."

"VCOSS looks forward to working with the Victorian Government over the coming months to help shape the next stage of this rollout to the benefit of all Victorians."

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 3:12pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 3:12pm

Is Brisbane 2032 next on the chopping block?

J

By Judd Boaz

So how much are the Brisbane Olympics really going to cost?

- Mike

It’s the right move, these events have become so crazy in costs that someone had to make a stand. Sydney is about to stage the Women’s Soccer World Cup but using established facilities. That should be the norm. Watch while Brisbane faces a huge bill for the Olympics it’s not sustainable.

- Rodney A Smith

While the 2026 Commonwealth Games have been scrapped for regional Victoria, the organising committee for 2032 Olympics said there are no such fears of a similar announcement in Queensland.

Brisbane 2032 chief executive Cindy Hook said she's confident the Games will come in on budget.

"I'm absolutely focused on the budget, the organising committee will be self funding and we have a long run way and more time than they did to plan, and I think that time if used well, will be very much to our advantage and I'm confident in our model," Ms Hook said.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 2:42pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 2:42pm

Opposition leader John Pesutto calls for accountability

J

By Judd Boaz

The opposition leader has blasted the government for what he called an "unprecedented cancellation" of a major event.

John Pesutto put Jacinta Allan — who served as Minister for Commonwealth Games Delivery — firmly in the firing line.

"If ministerial accountability means anything in Victoria … someone would be held responsible and accountable," Pesutto said.

"Victorians will need to be told why it is that Deputy Premier Allan should keep her job."

Pesutto called for transparency into the finances of the Commonwealth Games, saying that Daniel Andrews had provided "no real answers" as to the discrepancy in cost figures.

"How is it that the budget papers can be signed off by anybody at $2.6 billion, with the Premier out today saying they could cost as much as $7 billion?" he said.

"He's led everybody along and then he's been caught out because the numbers got away from him."

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 2:28pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 2:28pm

Shock announcement catches Victorians unawares

J

By Judd Boaz

The announcement today by Premier Daniel Andrews to withdraw from hosting the Games certainly caught many Victorians by surprise.

Commonwealth Games Australia chief executive Craig Phillips said he only found out via phone call at 6:30am this morning, while Greater Shepparton mayor Shane Sali waited until 9:30am to hear the news.

The website for the Games remains live, advertising the tournament for 17-29 March, 2026.

There are even tenders still online for consultants and project managers needed to supervise the construction of athletes' villages across regional Victoria.

It's safe to say the vast majority of Victorians were blindsided by today's press conference.

Tue 18 Jul 2023 at 2:20pmTue 18 Jul 2023 at 2:20pm

Netball Australia gives their take

J

By Judd Boaz

Netball Australia chief executive Kelly Ryan said although the body was disappointed, it had accepted the decision made by the Victorian government to scrap the Games.

"We understand and respect the decision made by the Victorian Government today," Ms Ryan said.

"We will continue to work closely with Commonwealth Games Australia as they explore suitable alternatives for the 2026 Commonwealth Games."

Australia's Diamonds are the reigning gold medallists at the Commonwealth Games, defeating Jamaica in Birmingham in 2022 to claim Australia's historic 1000th gold medal.
